is suggested by:

options.A: the discovery of figurines made from clay at the Trinil site.
options.B: recovery of a shell at the Trinil site with an intentionally engraved series of lines.
options.C: the use of complex tools requiring a high level of cognitive function.
options.D: cave paintings and elaborate burials with numerous grave goods at the Trinil site.

questions.stem_text:
When the Spanish explorer Hernando de Soto crossed a portion of the North American
continent, his expedition encountered direct descendants of which people?
questions.answer_explanation: The correct answer is the Mississippian people because Hernando de Soto's expedition in the 1540s encountered advanced societies in the southeastern United States that were part of the Mississippian culture, known for their complex mound-building and agricultural practices.

questions.stem_text:
The skulls of the earliest migrants to the New World do not match those of modern Native
Americans. This suggests that:

options.A: the early migrants were not human.
options.B: the early migrants did not contribute to the genetic pool of modern Native Americans.
options.C: the early migrants were a separate species.
options.D: craniometrics is an unreliable method of tracking populations.
options.E: skull shapes can change dramatically over generations.

questions.answer_explanation: The mismatch between the skulls of early migrants to the New World and those of modern Native Americans indicates that craniometric measurements may not accurately reflect genetic or population continuity over time, thus questioning the reliability of this method in tracing demographic changes.
